narrative.overview:
The house advertises its remedies. Each project is a 1910 elixir poster: a real image in an Art Nouveau window, a true claim in confident poster voice, a round stamp and two plain actions. The posters are pasted onto a wall beside a sticky house masthead, and the rest of the page keeps the same printed vocabulary: section titles are enamel stop signs, the journey and the navigation are tram route strips, and the project map is a network plan of four invented lines laid over a simplified Zürich zone-110 tram network.

The energy is the 1910 World's Fair and elixir advertising: luminous, sure of itself, a little tongue-in-cheek, as a genre and never as a copy of any game, brand or transit operator. Around the posters the scaffold stays modern and quiet: a sky-white ground, navy ink, generous section spacing, a grotesk for every sentence a visitor actually needs to read. Colour and period voice live on the printed objects (posters, ad, plan, closing poster); the page itself never dresses up.

Two theme names come from the cinema bill: the light **Matinée** is the default, the dark **Evening show** sits under `data-theme="dark"`. Printed objects keep their colours in both.
keyCharacteristics: Printed objects on a modern ground: posters, the training-tonic ad, the network plan and the closing poster carry full-strength fields; everything else is navy (or ivory) text on a calm ground.
Three voices of type: Bodoni Moda italic for names, Big Shoulders Display caps for claims and labels, Schibsted Grotesk for reading.
Gold double rules with small Jugendstil corner curls frame every printed object.
Transit grammar for structure: stop dots, route strips, lettered line discs, a zone border.
One authored motion moment (the paste-up) plus a hover straighten and a one-time line draw on the plan.

rules.name: The Printed Field Rule
rules.body: Posters, the ad, the photo mounts, the network plan and the closing poster are printed objects: their fields, inks and rules are fixed and do not swap with the theme. Only the page ground, page text, rules, ribbon and link colour change.

rules.name: The Six Fields Rule
rules.body: A poster is printed on exactly one of six fields: cobalt, vermilion, viridian or navy (ivory text, pale gold rule) or paper or sky (navy text, gold or navy rule, vermilion stamp). No gradients, no new field colours.

rules.name: The Four Lines Rule
rules.body: The plan has four lines, one per field of work, named by a letter, never a number, and drawn in the colour of the Zürich tram that runs its corridor: D (Data & ML) magenta like tram 10, V (Visualisation) black like tram 7, R (Research) green like tram 3, T (Tools & web) blue like tram 4 (tokens --tram-magenta, --tram-black, --tram-green, --tram-blue; the only colours outside the poster palette). Line discs repeat these colours wherever a stop is referenced (poster stop tags, map card).

rules.name: The Readable Hairline Rule
rules.body: Bodoni Moda is set with optical sizing off and `'opsz' 14` on the body. Its display optical size has hairlines too thin to read (Huber reads as Iluber); never switch optical sizing back on.

rules.name: The Facts In Grotesk Rule
rules.body: Every recruiting-relevant fact (role, employer, dates, degrees, results, contact) exists as plain grotesk or label text that can be read and copied. Bodoni and the poster voice decorate; they never carry the only copy of a fact.

rules.name: The No Mono Rule
rules.body: No monospace face anywhere. The site is not a terminal.

rules.name: The Paste-Up Tilt Rule
rules.body: Printed objects hang slightly askew (posters 0.8 to 1.5deg, wide bills -0.5deg, the ad -1.2deg, closing poster -0.6deg, photos about ±0.9deg). Interface elements (nav, buttons, text blocks) are never tilted.

dos: Do advertise every project as a remedy with a true, slightly tongue-in-cheek claim on one of the six fields, with a stamp and real demo/code actions.
Do frame every printed object in the gold double rule with its Jugendstil corners.
Do keep printed colours fixed across Matinée and Evening show; change only ground, text, rules, ribbon and link colour.
Do set every recruiting-relevant fact (role, employer, dates, degrees, results, email, GitHub, LinkedIn, ORCID) as plain, findable text.
Do keep achievements subtle: numbers live in captions, descriptions and the one small ad.
Do keep sport a marginal footnote at the end of About, after the work facts.
Do use the transit grammar (stop dots, route strips, line discs, zone border) for structure, with invented lines and the four poster inks.
Do keep copy in `src/data/content.js` with EN/DE parity, Swiss spelling and du in German.
Do honour reduced motion: posters simply appear and the plan lines are drawn from the start.
donts: Don't make it look like a newspaper: no newsprint columns, datelines, bylines or broadsheet rules.
Don't copy BioShock Infinite: no logos, characters, typography lockups, slogans or props from the game. The 1910 World's Fair mood is a genre only.
Don't use real transit branding: no VBZ or ZVV logos and no real line numbers. The route map borrows only the Zürich tram line colours (owner's decision).
Don't fake material: no paper grain, stains, torn edges, halftone noise or aged textures.
Don't add swing timing or extra electro-swing props (no gramophones, bouncing reveals, cabaret ornaments). The paste-up and the line draw are the only authored motion.
Don't put a metric hero, stats strip or achievement badges on the page.
Don't use monospace, glows, grid backgrounds, or kickers and eyebrows above headings.
Don't tilt interface elements or body text; only printed objects hang askew.
Don't turn Bodoni Moda's optical sizing back on.
